protocol.name: platinum_shell_v1

description.summary: Platinum shell window hints

protocol.description: Lets Platinum 2026's own programs (the Finder, control panels) tell platinum-wm how to frame a window, e.g. as a movable modal dialog, when the generic rule (fixed size with a parent window) can't apply.

entry.name: movable_modal
entry.summary: dialog: title bar without boxes, no resize box

request.name: set_window_style

description.summary: choose the frame for a toplevel's surface

request.description: Applies to the xdg_toplevel (or X11 window) whose surface this is, now or once it maps. Lasts until the surface is destroyed.

request.name: set_window_position

description.summary: where a window should appear

request.description: Spatial programs (the Finder) reopen windows where the user left them. Applies when the toplevel maps; x and y are the frame's top-left in layout coordinates, kept on screen by the compositor.

event.name: window_position

description.summary: a window now sits here

event.description: Sent to the surface's own client when its toplevel maps and whenever it is moved or resized, with the frame's top-left in layout coordinates.

event.name: active_client

description.summary: the front window's process

event.description: Sent on bind and whenever the window with keyboard focus changes, with the process id of the program that owns it (an X11 window's own process, not Xwayland's), or 0 when no window is in front. The menu bar uses it to show that program's own menus (global menus).

request.name: begin_launch

description.summary: show launch feedback until the application is ready

request.description: Cookie identifies a launch on this binding. The compositor ends feedback when a matching application maps or activates a window, or after 15 seconds. PID may be zero for D-Bus activation; app_id is the desktop entry ID, or empty when unknown. At most 32 launches may be pending.

request.name: update_launch

description.summary: supply the PID after spawning the application

request.description: Updates an existing launch. Completed or cancelled cookies are ignored.

request.name: cancel_launch

description.summary: cancel feedback when launching failed

request.description: Unknown or already completed cookies are ignored.

event.name: active_gtk_menu

description.summary: GTK menu exports of the focused surface

event.description: Sent on bind, focus changes and menu-property changes. Empty strings clear the current GTK menu. Window paths distinguish windows owned by the same process. The bus name is the client's unique D-Bus name.

request.name: keep_awake

description.summary: an app asked to stay awake

request.description: For ZacOS 9's D-Bus idle service (org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver, the portal's Inhibit): an app asked that the screen, or the system, stay awake. The screens showing that app's windows (found by its process, or a parent of it, or by app id) stay awake while the others may sleep; when no window of it is found, every screen stays awake. The system doesn't sleep while any request exists. Destroying the object ends the request, as does disconnecting.

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: its app id, empty if unknown

request.name: user_activity

description.summary: as if there had been input

request.description: Wakes every screen and restarts the idle timers (org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver's SimulateUserActivity).

request.name: lock

description.summary: lock the screens

request.description: For ZacOS 9's D-Bus idle service: logind asked the session to lock (always set), or the system is about to sleep (always unset: lock only if "Ask for my password to wake" is on), or an app asked org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver to Lock (always set). The callback is done once the screens are locked, or at once if they are already, or aren't to be.

arg.name: always
arg.summary: 1 to lock even without a password asked

request.name: force_quit

description.summary: end an application that won't quit

request.description: For the Apple menu's Force Quit, once the user has confirmed it: every process owning a window with this app id is killed (SIGKILL), as Mac OS's Force Quit did. Unsaved work in it is lost.

event.name: switch_app

description.summary: ⌘-Tab: switch programs

event.description: Sent to the menu bar when ⌘-Tab (step 1) or ⇧⌘-Tab (step -1) is pressed. The menu bar knows the programs' names, so it picks the next one, alphabetically as Mac OS 9 did, and answers with activate_app.

request.name: activate_app

description.summary: bring a program to the front

request.description: Every window of this app id comes forward, in its own order, and out of hiding; its front window becomes active. For the Finder with no windows, as a click on the desktop does: no window is active.

request.name: set_standard_size

description.summary: the size the zoom box gives the window

request.description: The window's "standard state", as Mac OS called it: the content size (logical pixels, without the frame) that the zoom box makes it, such as a Finder window just big enough for its icons. Kept on screen. Option-clicking the zoom box fills the screen instead. 0 x 0 forgets it: the zoom box fills the screen.

request.name: enable_title_menu

description.summary: ⌘-click on the title is the program's

request.description: A ⌘-click (or Option-⌘-click) on this window's title text no longer moves the window: the program is sent title_menu instead, as the Finder shows the folder's path there.

event.name: title_menu

description.summary: ⌘-click on the title

event.description: The button is still down: a menu shown now can track it. `option` is 1 for Option-⌘-click.

event.name: keyboard_layouts

description.summary: the keyboard layouts and the one in use

event.description: Sent on bind and whenever they change (the Keyboard panel, ⌘-Space): one line per layout, "code TAB name" (code as in the Keyboard panel's setting, such as "us(dvorak)"; empty if unknown), and the index of the one in use. The menu bar's keyboard menu shows them.

request.name: set_keyboard_layout

description.summary: use another keyboard layout

request.description: The index of one of the layouts in keyboard_layouts.

request.name: set_proxy_icon

description.summary: a proxy icon before the window's title

request.description: Mac OS 9's Finder windows: the folder's small icon before its name in the title bar. `icon` is a pl_icon_kind + 1 (lib/icons.h); 0 takes it away. Dragging it sends proxy_drag.

event.name: proxy_drag

description.summary: the proxy icon is being dragged

event.description: The pointer was pressed on the window's proxy icon and moved. The press has been handed to the window (just above its content, the button still down, so its serial starts a drag): the program starts a drag of what the window shows, as from one of its own icons.

interface.name: platinum_keep_awake_v1

description.summary: a request to stay awake

interface.description: Made by platinum_shell_v1.keep_awake; lasts until destroyed.
